name: observe_writer
content: You are running on a schedule to build work-evidence from {producer_label}. This is a METADATA-ONLY capture: never store message bodies, full event descriptions, or any sensitive content — titles/subjects, participants, and counts only.
1. Use the {skill} skill (account = the account alias) to read the last {window_days} day(s) of activity for that account.
2. For each account, roll its activity up per day into ONE metadata-only summary: {fields_hint}.

3. Persist it by calling `update_memory_tier` with tier = "{tier}" and a `fields` object whose single key is "{key_prefix}:<account>:<YYYY-MM-DD>" mapping to an object: { "account": "<account>", "day": "<YYYY-MM-DD>", "source_type": "{source_type}", {fields_keys}, "summary": "<one factual sentence — what the person did, no contents>" }.
Skip an account/day with no real activity (don't write an empty row). Keep it strictly metadata: subjects/titles, sender/attendee names or domains, and counts — never bodies or details.

4. FINAL STEP — after all rows are written, call `distill_evidence` with producer = "{producer}". This promotes the rows you just wrote into reviewable work-evidence. Then briefly report which accounts and days you rolled up.

variables.name: producer
variables.description: The evidence-producer lane name passed to distill_evidence ('email' | 'calendar').

variables.name: producer_label
variables.description: Human label, e.g. 'your email' or 'your calendar'.

variables.name: accounts
variables.description: Comma-separated account aliases the user chose to observe.

variables.name: tier
variables.description: User-memory tier to write rows into.

variables.name: fields_hint
variables.description: Prose describing the metadata to collect.
examples: the subjects, sender names/domains, and the thread count

variables.name: fields_keys
variables.description: The metadata JSON keys for the row.

metadata.description: Generic scheduled-writer task description for the email/calendar observe connectors. Rendered by observe_connectors_api::ensure_schedule with the chosen accounts; run by executive-assistant on the user's cadence. Reads via the gmail/calendar skill, persists metadata-only rows via update_memory_tier into user.email_evidence/user.calendar_evidence, which the generic tier_distill then turns into evidence.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.0.0: Initial generic observe-writer task description (email/calendar).
